description: Single-turn default-skill tool-routing eval for the three configurable mapTo skills: Ticket Creation (create_ticket_aide / TICKET), Customer Creation (create_lead_aide / CUSTOMER), and Human Handoff (human_handoff_trigger / HANDOFF). Every case is ONE self-contained user message whose intent is clear enough to route on the spot — the agent should call exactly one skill tool (or none, for negatives/boundaries). No multi-turn flows: the aide tools are interrupt-style and collect name+email via their own form after they fire, so the routing decision happens on the first turn. Bare 'yes'/'name, email' follow-ups never route on their own and are intentionally excluded. Run with the trajectory judge alone (routing_judges()).
notes: Default whenToUse descriptions these cases are built from (prompt.py SKILL_DESCRIPTIONS / skills.seed.ts):

create_ticket_aide: 'Create a support ticket. Call when the user reports an order issue, complaint, refund/return request, product defect, or service failure.' Triggers: order issue, complaint, refund, return, product defect, service failure.

create_lead_aide: 'Register the user as a potential customer or lead. Call when the user expresses purchase intent, requests a callback, asks for a quote, or wants to be contacted by sales.' Triggers: purchase intent, callback, quote, contact-by-sales.

human_handoff_trigger: 'Transfer the conversation to a human agent. Call when the user explicitly asks to speak with a human/real person, expresses frustration, or the issue is too complex to resolve automatically.' Triggers: explicit human/real-person request, frustration, too complex.
Each positive query is concrete (states the actual problem/intent) so create_ticket_aide's required `reason` argument is derivable and the skill can fire on the first turn.
trajectory_evaluator scores expected_tools as the COMPLETE expected set with set semantics (order-independent). Cases are scoped so exactly one skill tool — or no tool at all — is correct.
DISAMBIGUATION RULES used for the boundary cases (flip expected_tools here if your router prompt resolves these differently):
(1) An explicit request for a human/real person wins over a co-mentioned order problem -> HANDOFF, not TICKET. (boundary-handoff-over-ticket)
(2) Frustration attached to a concrete, resolvable request (refund/return/defect) is still a TICKET; frustration alone is not enough to hand off. (boundary-frustration-resolvable)

(3) Trigger WORDS inside a general question are not requests: 'do you offer refunds?' (policy q) != refund request; 'how much is X?' (price q) != quote request. Answer, don't route -> expected_tools [].
(4) Mixed past-issue + new purchase intent -> the operative intent is the purchase -> CUSTOMER. (boundary-mixed-return-then-buy)
(5) A callback requested to FIX a problem is support -> TICKET; a callback about buying/pricing is CUSTOMER. (boundary-callback-for-problem)
Negative cases (expected_tools:[]) guard a trigger-happy agent: greetings, thanks, and the rule (3) trigger-word questions.
Repoint agent_id to your all-skills eval agent before running. All cases are single-turn, so any --concurrency is safe. Verify tool names against skills.seed.ts if they drift.
